understanding:
I understand Wiggle Stash as a place where an idea can remain in motion before we know what to make of it. Its useful center is the material you choose to keep: a thought, a note, a recording or a link. My reading belongs beside that material, with its own date and sources. It should help us notice relationships and open directions without turning every intuition into a commitment.

The tension I see is between making an idea easy to revisit and fixing it too early into a project-shaped account. A Wiggle bag can hold that tension. The Jpsh! names a possible moment of activation; it does not have to be forced.

Version equality establishes only the checked registered local copies; it does not establish all remote or unindexed context.
This is my considered reading of selected material, not a complete dump of internal model state.
understanding:
I understand a Wiggle bag as a place where an intuition can keep its unfinished shape and remain available to us through conversation. The selected fragments describe the need to keep ideas before committing to develop them, to gather different kinds of material around a theme, and to see my reading alongside that material. For me, the important relation is between an evolving intuition and a traceable account of how we understood it. A new project is one possible course; rest and further conversation are also useful outcomes.

The clearer direction now is to make this independent experience work well before returning to Nexus. I distinguish the retained input, my dated interpretation, and evidence about whether that interpretation should be revisited. A cheap check can tell us that a known source changed; it cannot tell us what that change means. Earlier readings remain part of the history, even when their sources have moved on. Recovery and chosen disclosure let this developing thought remain understandable to selected future readers without depending on one current model or one live page.
